title: Ruby Bridges, 1960 — the six-year-old who walked in alone
sources: Wikipedia: Ruby Bridges — the first African American child to attend the formerly whites-only William Frantz Elementary School in New Orleans, on November 14, 1960, aged six; escorted by U.S. Marshals; "Driving up I could see the crowd, but living in New Orleans, I actually thought it was Mardi Gras"; white parents pulled their children out and all the teachers except one refused to teach; Barbara Henry, from Boston, taught her alone for over a year "as if she were teaching a whole class"; every morning one woman threatened to poison her and another held up a black baby doll in a coffin, so the marshals let her eat only food from home; her father lost his job, the grocery store would no longer let the family shop there; neighbours, black and white, walked behind the marshals' car; on July 15, 2011 she met President Obama at the White House, who told her "if it hadn't been for you guys, I might not be here"
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1969 Apollo 12 launches; 1910 Eugene Ely makes the first takeoff from a ship

Photos (public domain): U.S. Marshals with Ruby Bridges, 1960 (Department of Justice); a protest against school integration, Little Rock, 1959; soldiers escorting the Little Rock Nine, 1957; a Citizens' Council flyer, New Orleans, c. 1963; Ruby Bridges and President Obama, 2011 (White House, painting blurred). The 1964 Rockwell painting is not shown
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): empty classrooms

post.facebook:
On this day in 1960, six-year-old Ruby Bridges walked into William Frantz Elementary School in New Orleans — the first Black child at the formerly whites-only school.

Federal marshals escorted her past the crowd. "I actually thought it was Mardi Gras," she later said. White parents pulled their children out, and every teacher except one refused to teach her. Barbara Henry, from Boston, taught her alone for over a year, "as if she were teaching a whole class."

Every morning one woman threatened to poison her and another held up a black doll in a coffin, so the marshals let her eat only food from home. Her father lost his job, and the grocery store turned the family away. But neighbours, Black and white, found her father work, watched the house, and walked behind the marshals' car to school.

In 2011 she met President Obama at the White House. He told her: "If it hadn't been for you guys, I might not be here."

Also on 14 November: Apollo 12 launched (1969), and Eugene Ely made the first takeoff from a ship (1910).

youtube.description:
14 November 1960: six-year-old Ruby Bridges became the first Black child at William Frantz Elementary School in New Orleans, escorted by U.S. Marshals past an angry crowd. White parents pulled their children out and every teacher but one refused to teach her — Barbara Henry taught her alone for over a year. She was threatened with poison, her father lost his job, but neighbours walked behind the marshals' car to school. In 2011, President Obama told her: "If it hadn't been for you guys, I might not be here."

Also on 14 November: Apollo 12 launches (1969) and Eugene Ely makes the first takeoff from a ship (1910).
